text:
Marie Chen: heads-up — during the q5b int4 bring-up we observed a subtle label drift on the deid promptset after switching to the new tokenizer mapping. recall on the golden dropped ~6% on the sensitive-span suite.
Ajay Patel: can you paste the eval snippet and the exact commit that rolled?
Marie Chen: pasted below — run was with commit ff3a2b3 (token-map v2). eval diff: 
```
golden_recall: 0.912 -> 0.852
span_overlap_f1: 0.89 -> 0.74
most fails concentrated on newline/emoji-preserving spans
```
Simon K.: interesting — token span alignment issues often look like map/byte-pair boundary shifts, not model regression. did we also change normalize_unicode in the ingest?
Marie Chen: nope, normalize step unchanged. only token-map and quant kernel variant (int4-fast).
Rachel O'Neil: labelers flagged more "partial redaction" edgecases in the queue yesterday, thought it was annotator fatigue. could be tooling.
labeler-bot: @channel 12 tasks reassigned to deid-team for micro-review (task-ids: 6562,6563,6564).
Ajay Patel: let's do a micro-canary rollback: revert token-map v2 -> v1 on a small pool and rerun the golden slice. if recall returns, it's token-map. if not, next is quant kernel.
Marie Chen: running curate-cli rollback --token-map=v1 --pool=canary-small now. will post results in ~20m.
Simon K.: also record tokenizer token counts for the failing samples: `curate-cli inspect --ids 6562,6563,6564 --show-tokens` — want to compare boundary splits.
Marie Chen: output attached (trimmed):
```
6562: ["John", "\u200b", "Doe", "<REDACTED>"]
6563: ["Hello", "😀", "\n", "Address", "#", "123"]
6564: ["Street", "Apt", "#", "5B"]
```
Rachel O'Neil: those zero-width chars + emoji probably caused a split difference. our labeler UI treats ZWJ combos differently than the new tokenizer mapping.
Ajay Patel: if rollback fixes it, we should add a preflight check in model bring-up: compare tokenization diffs on the golden set and auto-fail if >5% token-boundary mismatch.
Simon K.: +1. propose a lightweight gate: `curate-cli token-diff --base=token-map:v1 --candidate=token-map:v2 --golden=golden-deid` that outputs per-sample diffs and a summary metric.
Marie Chen: rollback complete. rerunning golden eval on canary pool.
labeler-bot: job 9821 (golden-scan) started on canary-small.
Marie Chen: preliminary numbers: golden_recall 0.915 (v1) vs 0.853 (v2) on the same slice. span_f1 restored to 0.88. looks like token-map v2 is the culprit.
Rachel O'Neil: ok, immediate action: (1) pin token-map=v1 for q5b bring-up; (2) create a tiny golden-focused regression test for token-boundary-sensitive cases (ZWJ, emoji, newlines); (3) schedule a label UI audit to ensure any tokenizer change is reflected in annotator tooling.
Ajay Patel: I'll open a PR to pin v1 and add the `token-diff` preflight. Marie — can you draft the golden testcases and drop them in `gs://curation/gold/token-boundary-suite`?
Marie Chen: on it. dropping the first 40 cases now. will ping when uploaded.
Simon K.: long term we should avoid token-map surprises by adding a mandatory mapping-compatibility step to model onboarding checklist. otherwise quant wins at the cost of label stability. :thinking_face:
Rachel O'Neil: agreed. also looping in docs/labeling so they can add notes about ZWJ/emoji behavior.
Marie Chen: uploaded suite and PR linked here: https://git.internal/redwood/curate/pulls/1427 — includes examples, expected token splits, and a `ci-token-diff` job.
Ajay Patel: nice. tagging @eng-runtime to flag quant kernels for optional opt-in until token-map compatibility is ensured.
Marie Chen: thanks all. follow-up: retrospective tomorrow 10am to decide whether to revise token-map v2 or retire it. adding agenda to calendar. :calendar:
